description_full: Gerdau S.A., together with its subsidiaries, operates as a steel producer company. It operates through Brazil Business, North America Business, and South America Business segments. The company offers rebars, bars, wires, thick plates, hot rolled coils, billets, blooms, plates, wire rods, and structural profiles. It also provides special steel products for agricultural, automotive, construction, distribution, energy, industrial, and mining markets. In addition, it operates mines that produce iron ore located in Brazil. The company was founded in 1901 and is headquartered in São Paulo, Brazil.

financial_summary: Gerdau S.A. is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $8.6B market cap on $12.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -8% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 19% against a 10% cost of capital — a 10-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 14% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $237M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 5.63× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -8.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 1.8× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
